searchText: That isn't the best policy IMO If we wanted to move forward with this EIP, someone would have to fork the original? That would be the way -- for whoever is taking the responsibility. Should we formalize a process to claim abandoned EIPs? (if there isn't one already) I think that if nobody wants to pick up championship there is nothing much to do. it just sits there. There's definitely a difference between championing and fixing a table in the EIP, but yeah If "fixing the table" amounts to "merely editorial" work then, yeah, I don't see that a new champion or fork is needed. But I don't see much point in fixing abandoned EIPs either 😉 So. A paradox. An EIP is a file named eip-*N*.md, where *N* is the EIP number. That number will be the PR number. The PR will ask to add that file to the repo. But how can that file have been named in first place? The old resolution was to open an issue to claim a number, given they are assigned from the same sequence. Fine with me. Create the PR with a placeholder name and then just click the edit button in GitHub to set the filename and header data. It's nice to find a way out of an infinite loop. Thanks. If the authors aren't responsive, the EIP is going to fall into stagnant state soon enough. Better to encourage the person who actually cares to create a copy that they are author of and will push through to final. The idea someone mentioned of auctioning off skipped/unused EIP numbers via NFTs is rapidly growing on me. It would solve the problem of people who really want a number causing problems. I would be fine with the money just being burnt, or it can go to a charity, or gitcoin grants, or paid EIP editors as in situations like this? or does it address number-sniping? Under this half baked idea, any number that hasn't been used and is in the past would be auctioned off. If there is no EIP-42 then one could bid on that, yes. "prestige" EIP numbers 😛
